project_type: Tauri desktop app (Rust backend workspace + React/TypeScript webview frontend). Hybrid local/cloud AI model orchestrator (agent-harbor).
build_system: Cargo with a MEMBERLESS workspace ([workspace] members = [] and every crate [workspace] exclude'd); each crate builds via --manifest-path crates/<c>/Cargo.toml. Frontend uses npm/vite. NEVER run `cargo fmt --all` (breaks the memberless workspace) - format per-manifest.
test_framework: Rust: per-crate `cargo test --manifest-path crates/<c>/Cargo.toml`. Frontend: vitest + React Testing Library with mocked `@tauri-apps/api/core` invoke and `@tauri-apps/api/event` listen.
build_command: Per crate: `cargo build --manifest-path hybrid-orchestrator/crates/<c>/Cargo.toml`. Frontend: `cd hybrid-orchestrator/frontend && npm run build` (tsc && vite build). NOTE: crates.io + npm are 403 in this INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox, so these cannot actually run here; they run in GitHub CI after push.
test_command: Per crate: `cargo test --manifest-path hybrid-orchestrator/crates/<c>/Cargo.toml`. Frontend: `cd hybrid-orchestrator/frontend && npm run test` (vitest). Cannot run offline (registries 403); runs in CI.
verification_instructions: CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs, per crate: `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/<c>/Cargo.toml --check`, `cargo build --manifest-path crates/<c>/Cargo.toml`, `cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/<c>/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --manifest-path crates/<c>/Cargo.toml`; and in hybrid-orchestrator/frontend: `npm run lint` (eslint), `npm run format:check` (prettier), `npm run test` (vitest), plus a `tauri build`. OFFLINE self-checks available in this sandbox: per-crate `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/<c>/Cargo.toml --check` (if cargo present) and, from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend, `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` (if node_modules present). If node_modules/cargo registry are absent, rely on exhaustive manual review for unused imports/vars, tsc-strict types, and vitest mock completeness.
snapshot_or_generated_files: None relevant to this task. (Icons are regenerated by a separate workflow; not touched here.)
setup_instructions: Frontend deps: `cd hybrid-orchestrator/frontend && npm ci || npm install` (blocked in sandbox by npm 403). Rust: no separate setup; per-crate cargo commands via --manifest-path (blocked by crates.io 403 in sandbox).
environment_constraints: INTEGRATIONS_ONLY sandbox: crates.io and npm return 403, no Tauri CLI, and NO live Ollama or cloud endpoint. You CANNOT run cargo build/clippy/test, eslint/tsc/vitest, tauri build, or reach real provider endpoints here. Real gates run in GitHub CI after push; final behavioral proof is the USER's built release (they have a live Ollama with qwen3:8b and real Kiro/Gemini keys). Because of this, VISIBLE DIAGNOSTICS are load-bearing: they turn the user's next report into a precise error string. Self-audit exhaustively for the failure classes that cost this project FOUR CI cycles last time: (i) clippy -D warnings (no unused imports; if you add/remove a use of a type, add/remove its import); (ii) eslint @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars (no unused TS imports/vars); (iii) tsc strict; (iv) vitest: every test that mounts <App/> or a picker/settings surface must have IPC mocks (`invoke`) returning well-formed shapes for ALL commands it calls, INCLUDING any new startup load() call to list_available_models (returns { models, errors }) and any new refresh calls.
contribution_requirements: New/changed Tauri commands must be added to generate_handler! (crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs) AND get a typed frontend IPC wrapper in frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts. serde boundary enums use camelCase. Everything must be rustfmt (per-manifest) and prettier clean. Do NOT `cargo fmt --all`. Do NOT push/tag/PR (the orchestrator publishes). Update the spec (.kiro/specs/hybrid-orchestrator/{architecture.md,tasks.md}).
key_patterns: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by reading the code): (1) frontend/src/state/providers.ts exposes load() -> listAvailableModels() (the list_available_models command) and sets { models, errors }; initial state models:[], errors:[]. load() is NEVER called on app startup and NEVER when the chat picker mounts. The ONLY non-test caller is ProviderKeysSection (Settings > Providers & Keys), via loadProviders. The chat picker components (features/model-selector/PerMessageOverrideControl.tsx, RoutingModeToggle.tsx, and features/agent-editor/DefaultRoutePicker.tsx) only READ useProvidersStore((s)=>s.models); nothing triggers a fetch. app.tsx's single top-level useEffect only opens the onCoreEvent subscription and fans events into each store's applyCoreEvent - it does NOT call any store's load(). Other surfaces DO load on mount of their own component: AgentEditor.tsx calls personas/tools load() in a useEffect; ToolManager.tsx calls tools load(); History.tsx calls loadConversations(). The providers store has no such mount trigger for the chat picker and no startup load. (2) providers.ts applyCoreEvent refetches on CoreEvent 'providersChanged', but the backend NEVER emits CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged - the variant in crates/orchestrator-core/src/events.rs carries #[allow(dead_code)] with comment 'no emitter wired yet (provider/model selector surface)'. So saving a key/runtime never triggers a refetch. NET EFFECT: the chat picker store starts empty and nothing ever fills it (unless the user opens Providers & Keys, which calls the SAME singleton store's load(), which DOES reflect into the chat picker - confirming the single-store instance). This one bug explains BOTH 'Ollama shows nothing' AND 'adding a cloud key does nothing', and why there was no error (load never ran, so no failed call to report). FIX ROUTE for refresh: route (a) is readily available - AppState.core_events is an UnboundedSender<CoreEvent> already used by commands (e.g. state.core_events.send(CoreEvent::McpStateChanged{..}) / McpError in commands.rs; spawn_connect takes it). So the mutation commands can emit CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged through state.core_events after a successful mutation, and the store already refetches on it. This is the cleanest, most consistent path (matches how MCP commands emit). The #[tauri::command] wrappers hold `state: tauri::State<AppState>` and delegate to _inner(&state, ...); emit in the wrapper (or pass state into _inner) after Ok. Command bodies to touch: set_cloud_provider (~L1061), clear_cloud_provider (~L1215), set_local_runtime (~L803), clear_local_runtime (~L955), import_embedded_model (~L2212), select_embedded_model (~L2226). Also consider load_embedded_model / unload_embedded_model which change which local model is active/loaded. Emitting is fire-and-forget: `let _ = state.core_events.send(orchestrator_core::CoreEvent::ProvidersChanged);` mirroring the existing McpStateChanged sends. When wiring the emitter, DROP the #[allow(dead_code)] on ProvidersChanged in events.rs (clippy -D warnings will otherwise flag the now-used allow... actually an unnecessary #[allow] is NOT a clippy error, but the comment says 'drop each one as its emitter is wired' - remove it to keep intent honest; verify no OTHER dead_code use remains). DIAGNOSTICS: ProviderEnumerationErrors component (features/model-selector/ProviderEnumerationErrors.tsx) already renders the store `errors` and is already placed in PerMessageOverrideControl (chat composer) and ProviderKeysSection - it was simply always empty because load() never ran in the chat context. Once startup load() runs, a failing Ollama/cloud provider populates errors and they render near the picker. ADD a lightweight always-available 'Refresh models' affordance near the chat picker (calls useProvidersStore.getState().load() / a store action) and/or a per-provider diagnostics line in Settings showing, per configured provider id, whether it enumerated and how many models (or the error). Keep display-safe (never render resolved secrets; the errors are already display-safe by construction per architecture Section 8.2/9.1).
